full_judgment: 8. Defendant No.1, who died during the pendency of the suit was initially contesting the suit by filing a written statement. Thereafter, his son, defendant No.2 contested tine suit denying the material claims and allegation= made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit land did not belong to Pulin Bihari alone and he never made any gift nor did Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj ever accept any gift from him and thus, the said deed of gift is false, inoperative and was never acted upon. Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj purchased the land with his own money vide Certificate Case No.260 of 1950-51 and was inducted into the possession thereof on 11-5-1952 after obtaining a Boinama and accordingly, the Khatian was prepared in his name. Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj established an Ashram namely, Rhishidham on the said properties. The Shreeguru Sangha as claimed by the plaintiff had never any title and possession in the suit land. The land appertaining to plot No.77 of Schedule 1 belonged to Mahendra Das and after his death, his successors gifted the land in favour of Adwaitananda Puri in 1951. The land appertaining to plot Nos.31 and 19 of Schedule 1 was acquired by Adwaitananda Puri himself. The land appertaining to plot No.2523 of Schedule 2 was acquired on 7-11-1958 in the name of Sadananda, who was the Mohanta of Rhishidham. Later on, Sadananda Puri also obtained the land described in Schedule 2 to the plaint by various deeds and settlements. The lands of Schedules 1 and 2 belonged to Rhishidham which was established by Adwaitananda Puri. Mohanta Sadananda executed a Muktinama in favour of defendant No. 1. The suit land was never possessed by Shreeguru Sangha. Adwaitananda Puri never gifted his paternal properties. Noni Brahmacharini was never the Mohanta of Rhishidham but Sadanprida Puri was appointed Mohanta of Rhishidham by Adwaitananda Puri and then Sadananda Puri handed over the charge of Rhishidham to deceased defendant No.1. The plaintiff has filed the suit with the false and frivolous statements and allegations and hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
